question: What does the Canada National Parks Act say should come first when the minister manages a national park?
generated_answer:
The Minister shall maintain and make known a long-term plan for the maintenance and restoration of the ecological integrity of each national park of Canada. 

The Minister shall protect the natural resources of each national park of Canada, including its wildlife, for the benefit, education and enjoyment of the people of Canada or other persons resident in Canada, in a manner that will leave the resources unimpaired for the enjoyment of future generations.

The Minister shall take all reasonable means to fulfill the duty under subsection (1) and the duty under subsection (2) to maintain the ecological integrity of each national park of Canada and to protect the natural resources of each national park of Canada, including its wildlife, as if those duties were of equal importance.

The Minister shall allow persons to use those areas of the park for which they are suited in a manner that is consistent with the preservation of the ecological integrity of the park and the maintenance of the park's natural resources, if the use is consistent with the national policy of the system of national parks of Canada and the park's plan of management.

The Minister may enter into agreements to facilitate the management of the park and may, with the approval of the Governor in Council, expand the park by acquiring additional land.

The Minister shall undertake a public planning process to develop the plan of management for each national park of Canada and shall prepare a draft of the plan and make it available for public review.

The Minister shall take into account the views and concerns expressed during the public review, as well as any other relevant information, when finalizing the plan of management.

The Minister shall ensure that the plan of management is consistent with the national policy of the system of national parks of Canada.

The Minister may, in accordance with the regulations, take into account the benefits of tourism in the park when making decisions related to the management of the park.

The Minister shall monitor and assess the ecological integrity and the natural resources of each national park of Canada and take action to address any concerns or threats.

The Minister shall cooperate with other governments and organizations to support the management of national parks and the protection of natural resources.

The Minister shall support scientific research and public education to enhance understanding and appreciation of national parks and their ecological and natural resources.

The Minister shall ensure that all activities in a national park are conducted in a manner that is consistent with the protection of the park's ecological integrity and natural resources.

The Minister shall establish a system for monitoring and reporting on the state of the ecological integrity and natural resources of national parks of Canada.

The Minister shall make the results of monitoring and research available to the public to inform their understanding and support for the management of national parks.

The Minister shall take into account the role of national parks in supporting the cultural and spiritual well-being of Aboriginal peoples and shall cooperate with Aboriginal peoples in the management of national parks.

The Minister shall, in respect of each national park of Canada, establish a management board to provide advice on the management of the park.

The Minister may, by order, declare a national park of Canada or any part of it to be a wilderness area if the area is capable of providing a wilderness experience and its preservation in its natural condition is desirable.

The Minister shall ensure that any development or activity in a national park is consistent with the preservation of its ecological integrity and the protection of its natural resources.

The Minister may establish regulations for the purposes of this Act, including regulations respecting the use of national parks, the protection of wildlife, and the management of development and activities within the parks.

The Minister shall ensure that the management of national parks is subject to ongoing review and evaluation to ensure that the principles of ecological integrity and protection of natural resources are being met.

The Minister shall take into account the international commitments of Canada related to the protection of natural and cultural heritage when managing national parks.

The Minister shall support the development and implementation of ecological integrity indicators and monitoring programs to assess the health of national parks.

The Minister shall support the development of partnerships and collaborative approaches with other levels of government, Aboriginal peoples, local communities, and the private sector to support the management and conservation of national parks.

The Minister shall ensure that the management of national parks is transparent and open to public participation and that decisions are made with the benefit of science, traditional knowledge, and public input.

The Minister shall establish a process for the review and revision of the national policy of the system of national parks of Canada to ensure it remains relevant and effective.

The Minister shall ensure that the management of national parks is guided by the principles of sustainable development, including the integration of ecological, social, and economic considerations.

The Minister shall ensure that the management of national parks supports the achievement of Canada's international commitments related to the protection of biodiversity and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.

The Minister shall support the development and implementation of measures to address climate change and its impacts on national parks.

The Minister shall ensure that the management of national parks takes into account the potential impacts of human activity, including tourism, on the ecological integrity and natural resources of the parks.
